regions.full_page: of, I determined -- rain or shine -- train or no train, to go over to St. Mary's where Fr. Edward was assistant, and say Holy Mass and leave the rest to God. I had figured on catching the "Mil- waukee" scheduled to arrive from Seattle just an hour behind us, on the "N. P." but, we had lost thirty of those sixty minutes be- tween Minneapolis and the burned depot. The house-keeper at St. Mary's wondered that I was back so soon from the Solemnity. The Rt. Rev. Pastor was out on a sick- call, and I got to the Sacristy just in time for the last "Dominus Vobiscum", and final blessing of the 8 o'clock Mass. The young celebrant, too, was surprised at my early appearance; doubly so, on learning of my purpose to say Holy Mass and, even then, catch a train that day for Chicago. "If you were to start for the depot now, you might catch a train", he said, glancing at his watch, but, Thanks be to God, I said Holy Mass and made a short thanksgiving too. After breakfast, needless to say, no heavy one -- I lost no time in catching a trolley and getting over the half-mile or so to the station. "Is there any train for Chicago today?" I asked what seemed to be an official just waving a train backing in to stop. "Yes" he answered courteously "Here is one now". He hardly finished speaking, when, stopped was the train; on I stepped: and off went the "Burlington" at full speed; three hours late, its first stop at Point Douglas. I need not tell you what that meant to me. It took me past where I first saw the beauties of God's visible creation, down the Mississippi, where I played in the sand of its beautiful shore some four miles below; having crossed the mouth of the beautiful St. Croix and shot past Prescott where five of us had received Baptism. I certainly was not a tenth as grateful as I ought to have been, but I hope to be more so some day. I had reckoned, at all events, that it would please the Divine Lover of our poor souls and be good for mine especially to offer that Holy Mass; and that it would be a very easy thing for the Great God and Governor of the Universe to hold any train He might wish me to take. I hardly need to say that I asked HIM. Adored be His Holy Name! Now and forever. I do not remember that I was anxious about connections in Chicago, I probably was, more or less, seeing that we had to go so slowly in the rain, and for a time, through a fearful thun- derstorm. £ Just before reaching LaCrosse, we passed what seemed a victim of lightning, a burning farmhouse in the storm.
